newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi optimistic Eurostat will back Italian tax.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi optimistic Eurostat will back Italian tax.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday he was confident Eurostat would approve a one-off tax hike introduced to ensure Italy becomes a founding member of the planned single European currency.
Eurostat, the EU office responsible for overseeing government accounting practices, will rule on the so-called 'Euro Tax' later this week.
The levy is expected to raise 5.5 trillion lire ($3.3 billion) in 1997, but the government has promised to partially refund tax payers before the end of the century.
If Eurostat ruled that the tax was not a credible budgetary measure, Italy's chances of being a founding member of the single European currency would be blown out of the water.
Asked by reporters if he was optimistic the proposal would be accepted, Ciampi said "Yes...Wait a couple of days and all will be seen." -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
